758c195f136985b99848.text: Generalization is a written or a spoken statement in which you say or write

564eb6a2213d124523b3.text: that something is true to all the time when it is only true to some of the time.

f5accedaf3b0f0cbb8e6.text: Some generalizations are valid or true and some are faulty or invalid. Valid

776079546ffc62084389.text: generalization means true. It is supported by facts, agreed with what has been already known, used logic and reasoning, and proven with several examples. On the other hand, faulty generalization means false or invalid, which is not supported by facts and usually use these key words: none, all, always, never, everyone, and nobody.

fc3b80fab0d223aa83ac.text: There are some words that signal or give us a clue to recognize

d90063c9a34fe791d797.text: generalizations. These are: sometimes, always, never most, many, all, generally, seldom, and none.

rows: Some people like to have chocolate as their favorite dessert.
efff8a65c6b6643bbe66.text: Examples    Faulty Generalization Valid Generalization 1. All birds can fly. All birds have wings. 2. Chocolates is everyone’s favorite dessert. Some people like to have chocolate as their favorite dessert. 3. Everybody loves popcorn. Many people like popcorn. 4. Only teachers wear glasses. Many people wear glasses. 5. All cats have brown fur. Some cats have brown fur.
